subject.title: [Feature]: authenticate agent turn provenance across remote Gateways

question: Should remote agent-turn provenance be negotiated as server-authorized connection context or carried by a short-lived delegation credential bound to the authenticated device connection?
rationale: Current device authentication proves device identity but does not define delegated authority for a particular agent, session, turn, or delivery route; replay and rollout semantics require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Server-authorized connection context
options.body: Negotiate allowed agent and session provenance on the authenticated connection and attach a normalized read-only context server-side to every request.

options.title: Connection-bound delegation credential
options.body: Issue short-lived signed turn credentials with explicit audience, authority, expiry, nonce, replay, and reconnect rules.

options.title: Keep remote fail-closed
options.body: Retain denial and no-route behavior until a broader remote identity design is approved while local and plugin SDK work proceeds separately.

recommendation.title: Server-authorized connection context
recommendation.body: Negotiate allowed agent and session provenance on the authenticated connection and attach a normalized read-only context server-side to every request.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and recently maintained the local identity boundary, authored the linked security review, and currently owns the issue.
